items.prompt:
Read: "Nico packed his bag for the game. He put in his jersey, his shoes, and a towel. He left the house at six."
What did Nico put in his bag?
choices: His jersey, shoes, and a towel
items.why: The text says he put in his jersey, his shoes, and a towel.

items.prompt:
Read: "First, Ria swept the shop floor. Then she wiped the tables. After that, she opened the front door for customers."
What did Ria do right after sweeping?
items.why: "Then she wiped the tables" comes right after sweeping.

items.prompt:
Read: "The players were drenched after practice in the rain. Water dripped from their jerseys."
What does drenched mean?
items.why: Water dripping from their jerseys shows they were very wet.

items.prompt:
Read: "Because the bridge was closed for repairs, the school bus took the long road and arrived thirty minutes late."
Why was the bus late?
choices: The bridge was closed, so the bus took a longer road.
items.why: The sentence begins with "Because the bridge was closed," which is the cause.

items.prompt:
Read: "Marco kept looking at the door of the classroom. He checked the clock again and again. His lunch sat untouched."
How does Marco most likely feel?
choices: Anxious about someone or something arriving
items.why: Watching the door, checking the clock, and not eating are clues that he is nervously waiting.

items.prompt: Which word means almost the same as enormous?
items.why: Enormous and huge both mean very big.

items.prompt:
Read: "Bats help farmers. A single bat can eat thousands of insects in one night, including pests that damage crops. Some bats also pollinate fruit trees such as durian. Farmers who protect bat caves often see healthier harvests."
What is the main idea?
choices: Bats are useful to farmers in several ways.
items.why: The first sentence states it and the others give supporting examples.

items.prompt: The word misplaced is made of mis + placed. What does it mean?
items.why: The prefix mis- means wrongly, so misplaced means put in the wrong place.

items.prompt:
Read: "Both the jeepney and the tricycle carry passengers. However, the jeepney follows a fixed route, while the tricycle can go anywhere the passenger asks."
How are they DIFFERENT?
choices: The jeepney has a fixed route; the tricycle goes where asked.
items.why: "However" and "while" signal the contrast about routes.

items.prompt:
Read: "Join the coastal clean-up this Saturday! Every bag you fill saves a turtle. Bring gloves and your friends. Our beach deserves better."
What is the author's purpose?
choices: To entertain with a story about turtles
To persuade readers to join the clean-up
items.why: The commands ("Join", "Bring") and emotional appeal are meant to persuade.

items.prompt:
"The nurse checked the patient's pulse, then asked him to be patient while she prepared the medicine."
The word patient is used with two meanings. Which pair is correct?
choices: A sick person being treated; able to wait calmly
A doctor; a kind of medicine
items.why: First it names the person being treated; second it describes waiting calmly.

items.prompt:
Read: "The town's old market burned down in March. Vendors sold from tents for six months while the council raised funds. In September, a new concrete market opened with more stalls and a fire alarm system."
Which is the best summary?
choices: After the old market burned, vendors used tents until a safer new market opened six months later.
The new market has a fire alarm.
items.why: It covers the problem, the temporary fix, and the result without small details.

items.prompt:
Read: "I told everyone the new coach was useless. Three weeks later we won our first game in two years, and I had to admit, quietly, that I might have been wrong."
What does the first-person point of view reveal?
choices: The narrator's own bias and later change of mind
items.why: We see only the narrator's judgment and then the narrator's admission of error.

items.prompt: Claim: "Walking to school improves concentration." Which is the STRONGEST evidence?
choices: My cousin walks and gets good grades.
A study of 2,000 students found that walkers scored 8% higher on attention tests than those driven to school.
Walking is healthy, everyone knows that.
items.why: A large, measured study directly tests the claim; the others are anecdotes or opinions.

items.prompt: "The exam was a mountain, and I had no shoes." What does the speaker mean?
choices: The exam was held on a mountain.
The exam felt huge and the speaker felt unprepared.
items.why: The metaphor compares the exam to a mountain (hard to climb) and lacking shoes to being unprepared.

items.prompt:
Read: "Every evening Lola sorted the beans: good ones in the pot, bad ones to the chickens. When I asked why she didn't just cook them all, she said, 'Because the chickens also need to eat.'"
Which statement best expresses the theme?
choices: Even small acts of sorting can be acts of care for everyone who depends on you.
items.why: The theme is a general idea about life drawn from Lola's reason, not a fact from the story.

items.prompt: "Our neighbor got sick after the new cell tower was built, so the tower must be causing illness." What is the flaw in this reasoning?
choices: It assumes that because one thing happened after another, the first caused the second.
items.why: One case and a time sequence do not prove cause; other explanations are ignored.

items.prompt: "Congratulations to the committee on finishing the road only two years late and only twice over budget." What is the author's tone and purpose?
choices: Ironic criticism of the committee's poor performance
items.why: "Only two years late" is sarcasm; the words praise but the meaning criticizes.
